summary: West Africa's economic powerhouse and the entry point to the French-speaking African market. Abidjan is growing fast, has a stable Euro-pegged currency (CFA Franc), and is positioning itself as the gateway for investment across Francophone West Africa's 300 million people.
dataSource: Numbeo, Nomad List, US State Dept, Coworker.com

costOfLiving.currencyNote: The XOF (CFA Franc) is pegged to the Euro at a fixed rate, providing budget stability unusual for African cities. This is a meaningful advantage for long-stay planning.

internet.mobileQuality: 4G (Orange CI and MTN Cote d'Ivoire, 5G pilot in progress)
internet.reliabilityNotes: Internet improving rapidly. Fiber coverage in Plateau (CBD), Cocody, Marcory, and Riviera. Power can be intermittent in some areas. Major coworking spaces have generators.

safety.keyNotes: Abidjan requires neighborhood awareness. Cocody's Riviera and Deux Plateaux districts are relatively safe and are the primary expat and nomad zones. Motorcycle bag snatching exists citywide. Night transport should be via Uber or vetted drivers, not street taxis.

weather.drySeasonMonths: December to February and July to September
weather.rainySeasonMonths: March to June (long rains) and October to November (short rains)
weather.climateNotes: Hot and humid coastal climate. The December-February dry season is the most comfortable. Rainy season brings heavy downpours and occasional flooding in low-lying areas.

visaEase.usPassport: e-Visa required. Apply online. 90-day single entry approximately $73.
visaEase.nomadVisaNote: No digital nomad visa. Business visa or standard tourist visa required. Carte de Sejour (resident card) available for longer stays.
visaEase.specialNote: French-speaking comfort is essential. Abidjan operates almost entirely in French. Business, government, and daily life require French fluency or a local fixer.

notableCommunities: French expatriates (25,000-30,000, the largest French community in Africa outside North Africa)
Ivorian diaspora returnees from France and Belgium

keyFacts: Cote d'Ivoire has been the fastest growing economy in West Africa for most of the past decade, averaging 7-8% GDP growth annually
The CFA Franc is pegged to the Euro at a fixed rate, making Abidjan's cost structure predictable and immune to the currency volatility that affects Accra, Lagos, and Dar es Salaam
Abidjan handles most of landlocked West Africa's trade: Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, and Guinea all route a significant share of imports and exports through the port of Abidjan
The city has the largest French expatriate community in sub-Saharan Africa, which has built a support infrastructure (French schools, clinics, restaurants) that simplifies long stays
whyItMatters: Abidjan is the entry point for Francophone West Africa's 300 million person market. If your business or investment thesis involves the UEMOA (West African Economic and Monetary Union) zone, Abidjan is not optional. The CFA Franc's Euro peg is a rare gift in African finance: budget stability you can count on. The French expatriate infrastructure is the most developed in sub-Saharan Africa and makes settling in easier than it looks on paper. The tradeoff is language: Abidjan operates in French and English fluency alone will not carry you far. For the Afro-Francophone diaspora from France, Canada, Belgium, and Switzerland, Abidjan is the natural African base, increasingly attractive as the economy grows and infrastructure improves.
highlights: Gateway to Francophone West Africa market
